title: An exchange-assisted entangling gate between 87Rb and 171Yb Rydberg atoms
authors: Han Wang, Erdong Huang, Mingrui Jing, Hongshun Yao, Xin Wang, Jinguo Liu
abstract: Neutral-atom tweezer arrays support scalable quantum information processing. Dual-species $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$--$^{171}\mathrm{Yb}$ arrays combine long-lived ytterbium nuclear-spin data qubits with fast, species-selective rubidium ancilla control and readout. However, realizing interspecies gates without inducing destructive Stark mixing in divalent atoms remains an outstanding problem. Here, we identify an optically accessible $S{+}S\leftrightarrow P{+}P$ Förster resonance at zero electric field, providing strong dipole-dipole exchange at array pitch. Using a shaped optical pulse under finite control response, we demonstrate a $0.36\,μ\mathrm{s}$ exchange-assisted controlled-$Z$ gate with an intrinsic fidelity of $99.91\%$, remaining above $99.85\%$ under bounded perturbations. We also identify an auxiliary repulsive van der Waals channel, providing a comprehensive toolbox for hybrid quantum processors.
summary: This paper reports on the implementation of an exchange-assisted controlled-Z gate between $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ and $^{171}	ext{Yb}$ Rydberg atoms. By exploiting a specific Förster resonance, the authors overcome the challenge of Stark mixing to achieve a high-fidelity gate ($99.91\%$). This work advances the field of scalable quantum computation using neutral atom arrays.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is realizing high-fidelity interspecies entangling gates between different atomic species ($^{87}	ext{Rb}$ and $^{171}	ext{Yb}$) without suffering from destructive Stark mixing.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a controlled-Z gate with an intrinsic fidelity of $99.91\%$ using an exchange-assisted protocol.
method: The gate is implemented by shaping an optical pulse to drive the system through a specific Förster resonance, generating the necessary conditional phase shift.
model_or_system: The system uses a dual-species neutral atom array combining $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ (ancilla) and $^{171}	ext{Yb}$ (data qubit). The interaction is mediated by an optically accessible $S+S \leftrightarrow P+P$ Förster resonance.
key_observables: Intrinsic fidelity ($99.91\%$), gate duration ($0.36 \ \mu	ext{s}$), and the conditional phase $\Phi_{CZ}$.
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($|V|/h = 15.4 	ext{ MHz}$), separation distance ($R = 3.4 \ \mu	ext{m}$), and magnetic field strength ($B = 3.10 	ext{ G}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis initially uses a fixed-electronic-$m$ model, which is later extended to include hyperfine structure (HFS); the protocol relies on the strong coupling dominating over Zeeman shifts.
figures_summary: Figures characterize the Förster exchange channel, showing dependence on separation and field, and illustrate the optical excitation schemes and the resulting conditional gate phase accumulation.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first characterizing the microscopic Förster resonance and pair interaction, then detailing the three-stage pulse sequence required for the CZ gate, and finally quantifying the achieved fidelity under controlled conditions.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, high-fidelity protocol for building hybrid quantum processors using different atomic species, which is a major goal in quantum information science utilizing neutral atoms.
